newsitem.title: CHILE: Fugitive German hiding in Chilean colony -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive German hiding in Chilean colony -- paper.

text.p: The leader of a secretive German colony wanted on charges of child abuse is hiding inside the heavily guarded estate in southern Chile, a newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The evening paper La Segunda quoted two young men who escaped from the settlement last week as saying that Paul Schaefer was hiding inside Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony), 200 miles (320 kms) south of Santiago.
Police have raided the secluded colony hidden behind barbed-wire fences in the foothills of the Andes looking for Schaefer, but have found no traces of the fugitive leader.
Schaefer, 76, is the subject of an international arrest warrant after being accused of molesting boys at the colony.
Tobias Muller, a 24-year old German, and Chilean Gonzalo Luna told La Segunda that Schaefer was still in the colony.
Schaefer, who has not been seen in public in recent years, also faced charges of illegally detaining children, tax fraud and obstructing justice.
Former residents said they were not allowed to read newspapers or watch television, their mail was censored and youngsters were subjected to unusual punishments by Schaefer.
